overall: Violations found: the May 13 notice failed to name the nonunion personnel under Purpose 2, and the Committee signed the Superintendent's contract before the open-session vote. Other allegations declined; unraised minutes and roll-call issues flagged as reminders. Ordered compliance and member training; nullification declined.

allegations.summary: May 13 notice and executive session announcement did not name the nonunion personnel (the Superintendent) whose contract was being negotiated.
allegations.key_passage: By failing to identify her in the notice and in the announcement prior to entering executive session, the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee voted to renew the Superintendent's contract in executive session.
allegations.key_passage: the Committee essentially approved the contract in executive session, something we have consistently said a public body may not do.

allegations.summary: Committee signed the Superintendent's contract on May 20 before the open-session approval vote on June 10.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Committee executed the Superintendent’s contract prior to voting to approve it in open session, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee suppressed public comment and refused to provide or discuss the Superintendent's evaluation.
allegations.key_passage: Even if true, such allegations do not state a violation under the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Committee ratified the contract on June 10 without discussion and without letting the public see the contract.
allegations.key_passage: Nor does the Law require the public to see a contract before a public body votes to approve it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged notices should have listed an anticipated vote on the Superintendent's contract.
allegations.key_passage: We have consistently explained that it is reasonably foreseeable that a public body may take action and hold a vote following discussion of a topic listed on a meeting notice; the Open Meeting Law does not require that the notice separately indicate the possibility of a vote.

allegations.summary: Unraised issue: the 2026-2027 school start date was discussed in May 13 executive session and was not on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: This topic was not an appropriate topic for executive session unless it was part of a discussion that falls within the 10 allowable purposes for an executive session.

allegations.summary: Unraised issue: minutes of at least two meetings, including the April 15 retreat and May 13 executive session, lacked sufficient detail.
allegations.key_passage: We recommend that the Committee revise any minutes that do not include the requisite level of detail, including minutes of the April 15 retreat and of the May 13 executive session.

allegations.summary: Unraised issue: the May 13 roll call vote to enter executive session was recorded as unanimous rather than by roll call.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee is reminded that even unanimous votes must be recorded by roll call in the minutes.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of intent to violate.
All Committee members must attend an Open Meeting Law training webinar provided by the AG's office within 90 days of the letter and certify completion.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
